title: Trump Says Pro-Israel Groups Have Less Power in Congress
summary: Have you ever heard of lobbying? It's when groups try to convince politicians to support their ideas. For a long time, pro-Israel groups were super powerful in Washington, D.C. They could get many politicians to support Israel. But President Trump says that's changing. In a recent interview, he said that 20 or 25 years ago, these groups had the most powerful lobby in Washington. Now, he says, things are different. He pointed to Senator Chuck Schumer, who is Jewish and has always supported Israel. Trump said Schumer has "become virtually a Palestinian." That upset a lot of people. Jewish and Muslim groups said it was like using "Palestinian" as an insult. This isn't the first time Trump has said something like this. He said it in 2025 too. Schumer is the highest-ranking Jewish official in U.S. history. He usually defends Israel, but recently he criticized Israel's leader, Benjamin Netanyahu, for not doing enough to protect civilians in Gaza. He also said the war with Iran is a "fiasco." That means a complete failure. So what's happening? Some surveys show that support for Israel is going down, especially among young people and Democrats. Trump's comments show that even he sees the change. It's a big deal because the U.S. has been Israel's biggest ally for a long time. But things might be shifting.
why_it_matters: This story shows how leaders' words about identity and loyalty can affect how different groups feel respected or insulted in your own community.
